contract.goal: an administrative control acting on per-replica memory reaches every live replica through job-core's database (heartbeats, commands, acknowledgements), reports per replica, and evicting a cache everywhere is its first control, as specified in specs/replica-control and specs/cache-admin
contract.output: LudwigCacheRegistry.evictAll; job-core changesets (instance, command, ack); ReplicaControlPoller; ReplicaControl SPI + startup validator; /admin/v1/replicas, /controls/{control}, /commands/{id}; replicas + caches areas; cacheevict control; service grants; OpenAPI; docs EN+RU
constraints: the database is the only transport
a command targets the instances live at submission; a silent target is named, never counted done
at most once per process; controls idempotent
authorization by the control's own operation, via AdminAccessEvaluator; privileged needs Admin-Reason
liveness judged by the database's now()
done_when: mvn -pl :job-core,:cache-spring-boot-starter + all in-repo dependents -am verify (one reactor install)

decisions: before the first edit: the design's changesets 0002/0003 collide with job-core-0002-create-admin-approval (admin-four-eyes-approval); they become 0003-create-instance and 0004-create-control.

1.1: LudwigCacheRegistry gains evictAll(name) - the declared definition's cache (built on demand, so a replica that never read it still clears the shared tier) delegates to LudwigCache.evictAll(), which already invalidates local and publishes ALL_KEYS to the shared tier; an unknown name throws UnknownCacheException. It also gains settings() (resolved CacheSettings of every declared cache), which the design did not name but the caches listing needs for owner, purpose, tiers and TTL. CacheAutoConfigurationTest 8/8 (+1); ModuleIndependenceTest 2/2 (no in-repo dependency added). mvn -pl :cache-spring-boot-starter -am verify rc=0.

2.1: 0003-create-instance.sql (job_instance owner PK, started_at, last_seen_at, index on last_seen_at) and 0004-create-control.sql (job_control_command with JSONB arguments and TEXT[] targets, indexes on deadline and submitted_at; job_control_ack PK(command_id, owner), FK ON DELETE CASCADE so the purge deletes commands only), both included after 0002, git add -N; check_migrations 108 conforming.

2.2: ru.ludwigandreas.job.core.control (outside the ArchUnit-analysed admin package, beside lock/claim, because it is JDBC): ControlStore (heartbeat upsert, live by the database's now(), insert with targets TEXT[] and deadline now()+ack-timeout, pendingFor (deadline > now, owner = ANY(targets), no own ack), ack ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, bounded purge with cascade, forget unseen > 1 day); ReplicaControlPoller (SelfSchedulingLifecycle 'ludwig-replica-control', one per replica, not run-locked; in-memory applied-id set; handler on its own thread with handler-timeout; codes control-failed/-timeout/-result-too-large (4 KiB)/-unknown; purge every 30 passes under run lock 'ludwig-replica-control-purge'). ludwig.job-core.control.{enabled, poll-interval PT2S, ack-timeout PT30S, handler-timeout PT10S, retention P7D}.

2.3: ReplicaControl<A> SPI {name, argumentType, operationFor(A), possibleOperations, apply -> Optional result}; ReplicaControlValidator at startup (lower-case unique names, every possible operation catalogued). replicas area (read; operate/privileged reserved). ReplicaAdminService: bind JSON -> type (400), Jakarta validate (400), operationFor (IllegalArgumentException -> 400), AdminGrants.holds else AdminAccessEvaluator.refuse (403, published denial), privileged needs Admin-Reason (400), heartbeat self, targets = live now, insert, audit via a new public AdminAudit.record(AdminInvocation, ...) overload in the security starter (the binding is package-private). Envelope per design: any failed ack -> FAILED control-failed [owners]; all succeeded -> SUCCEEDED; deadline passed with silent -> FAILED control-unacknowledged [silent owners]; else RUNNING. Controller: GET /admin/v1/replicas, POST /controls/{control} (@AdminAuthenticated, 202 + Location), GET /commands/{id} (poll with Retry-After). ReplicaControlIT 5/5 - one context as replica A plus a second poller over the same Postgres as replica B (deviation from 'two contexts': same behaviour, one container): both apply once and SUCCEEDED with per-replica results and the audit naming targets; refusals record nothing (blank arg 400, missing op 403, privileged without reason 400, unknown control 404); silent replica named UNACKNOWLEDGED and FAILED; a throwing replica fails its entry and the command while the other applies; liveness within three intervals and a stale replica not targeted. ReplicaControlValidatorTest 2/2. job-core install 98 unit + 26 IT, 0 failures.
